thread:
maria-support: Hey @lee-cs — ACME Widgets (acct: acme-123) reporting a sharp spike in 429s starting ~02:03 UTC after last night's rate policy canary. Also seeing intermittent 401s. Can you paste any quick repro logs?

lee-cs: Repro logs from the customer (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 02:04:12 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 2187654980
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"error\": {\"message\":\"rate limit exceeded\"}
}
```
Also later:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":{"message":"invalid_token"}}
```
They say these 401s started appearing shortly after the 429 surge.

maria-support: Customer says they did not change anything client-side. They have a batch job that spikes (small bursts every minute).

jake-eng-platform: I pushed a canary last night: rollout id `policy-rollout-2026-03-15-02` — target 5% of traffic; changed standard plan to 60/min (was 120/min) to test burst protections. Deploy bot should have the event.

deploy-bot: policy-rollout-2026-03-15-02 deployed at 2026-03-15T02:00:14Z (canary 5%, limit: 60/min, burst: 10/sec).

sam-oncall: Can we confirm whether ACME was in the canary cohort? If yes, 60/min with burst 10/sec could explain repeated 429s if their job batches many requests within a minute. The 401s worry me — maybe token reuse/cache eviction?

jake-eng-platform: Checking mapping... one sec.
jake-eng-platform: ACME's traffic was flagged by the routing shard and appears in the canary cohort — approx 4.8% of their requests hit the canary shard due to their geo/edge hash.
jake-eng-platform: 401s look correlated with auth service errors we saw at 02:05 UTC in the auth pool; suspect token verification failures under retry/backoff. Not a direct result of rate limit change but timing overlaps.

lee-cs: From customer stack: they get a token, then fire ~30 parallel requests, some return 429 then a retry logic returns 401 on a retry attempt. So two simultaneous issues: tighter rate limit causing 429s, and retries getting stale/invalid tokens sometimes leading to 401s.

maria-support: Customer asking for immediate mitigation — can we pause/rollback canary or whitelist ACME? They have a paying subscription and this impacts billing/calls.

jake-eng-platform: Options: (1) pause/rollback the canary (fast, global change), (2) add ACME to `policy-exempt` list (targeted), (3) temporarily raise per-minute limit but keep burst cap. I'd vote for targeted exemption + short rollback if exemption takes longer.

billing-bot: Alert: ACME billing spike detected 02:04-02:10 UTC — usage meter +38% above baseline. Flagging for audit.

sam-oncall: Quick repro steps for eng-platform: please run `./infra/query-rate-events --customer acme-123 --since 1h --group-by=minute` and share any spikes. Also check auth pool logs `auth-service/*/error_rate` around 02:03-02:08 UTC.
jake-eng-platform: Running now... (results truncated)
```
minute, requests, 429_count
02:02, 42, 0
02:03, 520, 46
02:04, 510, 112
02:05, 48, 3
```
Auth errors: auth-service/region-2: increased token validation latency and occasional 500s 02:04-02:06.

jake-eng-platform: Given this, I'll add ACME to `policy-exempt` for the next 30m and trigger a rollback of the canary to stop further customers from being impacted. Can someone from ops approve immediate rollback?
sam-oncall: Approve. Do it.
maria-support: I'll notify ACME and open a support ticket with timeline + ask them to avoid retries >3 in bursts.

jake-eng-platform: Executing: `deployctl rollback policy-rollout-2026-03-15-02 --confirm`

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for rollout id policy-rollout-2026-03-15-02 at 2026-03-16T02:06:12Z. Status: in-progress.

(10m pass)

deploy-bot: rollback completed at 2026-03-16T02:15:02Z. Canary removed, global policy reverted to previous limits (standard: 120/min).

lee-cs: ACME confirms: errors subsided ~02:16 UTC, 429s dropped to baseline and no further 401s reported. Customer is relieved but requests root-cause writeup.
jake-eng-platform: Follow-ups: 1) Investigate auth service 500s during the window, 2) refine canary targeting logic (edge-hash causing partial cohort of a single customer), 3) consider per-customer grace buffer during policy rollouts (whitelist queue), 4) update rollout playbook to include immediate exempt path.
maria-support: I'll draft a post-incident note for customer and include temporary credits for the billing spike.
sam-oncall: Closing loop here — will open a tracking ticket for auth-service investigation (TKT-4581) and another for rollout-targeting (TKT-4582).

lee-cs: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
